title: Generate Synonym Query Rewrites (SWE Supplement)
prompt:
Implement `rewrite_queries(text, synonym_groups)`. Return every distinct sentence obtainable by replacing zero or more whole-word spans with another phrase from the same synonym group, sorted lexicographically. Include the unchanged sentence. A replacement consumes its span of the original sentence: words introduced by a replacement cannot be rewritten again. When spans overlap, choose one path or the other, never both over the same original words.

### Part 1: Single words

Each synonym group initially contains single words. Each original word may be left unchanged or replaced by another word in any group containing it.

### Part 2: Phrases and overlapping groups

A group may also contain multiword phrases, and a phrase may belong to multiple groups. Match a phrase only as a sequence of complete words. At each position, consider the unchanged original word and every matching group phrase that starts there. Deduplicate equivalent resulting sentences.

`text` and each group phrase contain alphabetic words separated by single spaces. Matching is case-sensitive. Each group contains at least two phrases; groups may overlap. Return `['']` for empty text.

example.output: ['email android', 'email iphone', 'email phone', 'outlook android', 'outlook iphone', 'outlook phone']
example.reasoning: The first word has two choices and the second has three. Their six distinct combinations are sorted.

references.label: Original SWE interview report — single-word and phrase synonym rewrites
Independent full-stack SWE report — multiword follow-up

background_note: The detailed SWE report specifies sorted unique outputs, whole-word matches, unchanged output, multiword phrases, overlapping groups, and no repeated rewrites. It does not settle whether shared phrases make entire synonym groups transitively equivalent; this practice version permits direct alternatives from each matching group only, without transitive closure. Case-sensitive matching and single-space input are also local choices. Its optional spacing-preservation part is outside this exercise. This is not a confirmed MLE question.
